title: The training principles series: slow negatives
summary: Answering a subscriber, NH explains why he does slow negatives and fast positives: slower reps increase difficulty and fiber damage, preserve form, and above all improve mind-muscle connection, since the muscle you feel stretching is the one you feel working. He lists exceptions: fast but controlled bench negatives, no deadlift negatives, slow positives on curls.

claims.claim: The common rationale for slow reps is more time under tension and more fiber damage; NH agrees only to a point, since travel distance stays the same and only tempo changes.
Lifting slowly does cause more muscle fiber damage and makes lifts much harder, e.g. tempo squats are harder than normal squats.
Lifting faster isn't wrong; it depends on goals and the lift.
Slow negatives preserve form; when he gets hyped and rushes negatives, his positive form suffers.
Squats are all about the negative for NH: if he controls the descent, he gets the weight up.
On bench, slow negatives never help his positive, so he lowers the bar fairly fast but controlled, with purpose using his lats, never bouncing.
He doesn't do negatives on deadlifts because it's a positive-only lift; don't be dogmatic that every lift must be slow.
The positive phase should be as fast and explosive as possible after a slow, tight negative.
Curls are the exception: a slow positive improves the squeeze at the top for any grip; the negative is slow with an EZ bar but fast with dumbbells.
Slow negatives aren't just for bodybuilders; anyone caring about injury prevention, form or muscle activation should try them.
Rushing the negative makes you rely on stronger muscles; going slow lets you feel the target muscle, e.g. fast push-ups hit front delts while slow ones let him feel the whole pec stretch.
The muscle you feel stretching and storing energy on the negative is the one you'll feel working on the positive; use slow squat negatives to feel glutes.
For poor lat mind-muscle connection, do very slow pull-ups with a full stretch; the muscle you felt stretching will do the pulling.
NH realized from watching his own videos that he always does slow negatives and fast positives, and will keep doing so.
